1.overview: Jesus appears to the apostles over forty days, teaches about God’s kingdom, promises the Holy Spirit, and ascends from the Mount of Olives. In Jerusalem, Peter explains Judas’s departure from the apostolic ministry, and the gathered believers choose Matthias to join the eleven apostles.

2.overview: At Pentecost, the Holy Spirit fills the disciples, who speak in other languages as Jews from many nations gather in Jerusalem and hear them declare God’s works. Peter explains the event through Joel and David, proclaims Jesus’ death, resurrection, and exaltation, and sees about three thousand people baptized as the believers form a growing community.

sections.heading: Peter Proclaims Jesus as Lord and Christ
The Crowd Responds and Is Baptized
The Believers Share a Common Life

3.overview: Peter heals a man lame from birth at the temple gate in Jesus’ name, and the crowd gathers at Solomon’s Colonnade as Peter explains that God glorifies Jesus, whom they reject and kill but raise from the dead. Peter calls the people to repent and turn back, citing Moses and the prophets as witnesses that the Christ suffers and that God appoints Jesus for the restoration and blessing of Israel.

4.overview: Peter and John are arrested for proclaiming resurrection in Jesus, then testify before the Jerusalem authorities that the healed man stands well through Jesus Christ and that salvation is found in no one else. After their release, the believers pray for boldness, are filled with the Holy Spirit, and share their possessions, including a gift from Barnabas.

5.overview: Ananias and Sapphira die after Peter exposes their deception, while the apostles perform signs and wonders and draw growing crowds in Jerusalem. After an angel releases them from jail, the apostles testify before the Sanhedrin that God raised and exalted Jesus, and Gamaliel persuades the council to release them after a flogging; they continue teaching and proclaiming Jesus as the Christ.

6.overview: A dispute over the daily food distribution leads the Twelve to appoint seven men, including Stephen and Philip, while they focus on prayer and the ministry of the word. The Jerusalem community grows, and Stephen’s signs and disputes with members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen lead to his arrest and accusations before the Sanhedrin.

7.overview: Before the Sanhedrin, Stephen recounts God’s dealings with Abraham, Joseph, Moses, and Israel, emphasizing Israel’s repeated rejection of God’s messengers and the Most High’s presence beyond a human-built temple. He accuses his hearers of resisting the Holy Spirit and betraying the Righteous One, then sees Jesus at God’s right hand as the council stones him, with Saul present.

sections.heading: The Tabernacle, the Temple, and the Accusation

8.overview: After Stephen’s death, persecution scatters the Jerusalem church, while Philip proclaims Christ in Samaria and Peter and John come to confirm the Samaritans’ reception of the Holy Spirit. An angel directs Philip to an Ethiopian official, whom he teaches from Isaiah and baptizes before continuing to preach from Azotus to Caesarea.

sections.heading: Philip in Samaria and Simon’s Offer

9.overview: Saul encounters the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus, receives his sight through Ananias, and begins proclaiming Jesus before escaping plots in Damascus and Jerusalem. Peter heals Aeneas in Lydda and raises Tabitha in Joppa, leading many to believe and bringing Peter to stay with Simon the tanner.

sections.heading: Saul Encounters Jesus on the Road
Peter Heals Aeneas and Raises Tabitha

10.overview: Cornelius receives an angelic instruction to summon Peter, while Peter’s vision and the Spirit’s direction prepare him to go to Caesarea and meet the Gentile household. Peter proclaims Jesus’ life, death, and resurrection; the Holy Spirit falls on the Gentile hearers, and Peter orders them baptized in Jesus’ name.

sections.heading: The Spirit Falls on the Gentiles

11.overview: Peter recounts to the Jerusalem believers his vision in Joppa and the Spirit’s direction to visit Cornelius, explaining that the Holy Spirit came upon the Gentiles just as it had upon Jewish believers; the church accepts that God has granted Gentiles repentance unto life. In Antioch, believers proclaim Jesus to Greeks, Barnabas brings Saul to teach the growing church, and the disciples send relief to Judea after Agabus predicts a famine.

sections.heading: Famine prediction and relief for Judea

12.overview: Herod executes James and imprisons Peter, but an angel frees Peter, who joins the praying believers at Mary’s house before leaving for another place as Herod searches for him. Herod dies after a dispute with Tyre and Sidon and a public address, while God’s word spreads and Barnabas and Saul return from Jerusalem with John Mark.

sections.heading: The Word Spreads and the Mission Returns

13.overview: The Holy Spirit commissions Barnabas and Saul from Antioch, and their mission through Cyprus leads the proconsul Sergius Paulus to believe. In Pisidian Antioch, Paul recounts Israel’s history and proclaims Jesus’ resurrection and forgiveness, after which opposition drives Paul and Barnabas from the region as the message spreads among the Gentiles.

14.overview: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas preach in the synagogue, face opposition, and flee to Lystra, where Paul heals a man and the crowd mistakes the apostles for gods. After Paul is stoned, they travel through the region strengthening churches and appointing elders, then return to Antioch and report how God opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

sections.heading: The healing and mistaken worship at Lystra
Paul’s stoning and the return journey

15.overview: A dispute over circumcision and the law leads Paul and Barnabas to Jerusalem, where Peter, Paul, Barnabas, and James address the inclusion of Gentile believers and the assembly sends a letter setting out essential requirements. The letter brings encouragement to Antioch, and Paul and Barnabas later separate over John Mark, with Barnabas sailing to Cyprus and Paul traveling with Silas through Syria and Cilicia.

sections.heading: The council’s letter goes to Antioch

16.overview: Paul recruits Timothy, delivers the Jerusalem decisions, and follows the Spirit’s direction to Macedonia, where Lydia and her household receive the gospel in Philippi. After Paul casts a spirit from a slave girl, he and Silas are beaten and imprisoned, but an earthquake leads the jailer and his household to believe and be baptized; the magistrates release them after learning they are Roman citizens.

sections.heading: The Call to Macedonia and Lydia’s Baptism

17.overview: Paul proclaims Jesus as the suffering and risen Christ in Thessalonica and Berea, where some believe and opponents drive him onward. In Athens, Paul declares the Creator God’s call to repentance and coming judgment through the appointed, risen man, prompting mixed responses.

sections.heading: Paul’s preaching and opposition in Thessalonica
Paul encounters Athens and its philosophers

18.overview: Paul works and preaches in Corinth with Aquila and Priscilla, receives the Lord’s assurance, and continues teaching despite opposition before Gallio dismisses the accusation against him. Paul travels through Ephesus, Caesarea, Jerusalem, and Antioch, while Apollos arrives in Ephesus, receives further instruction from Priscilla and Aquila, and later proves from Scripture that Jesus is the Christ.

19.overview: In Ephesus, Paul baptizes about twelve disciples of John in Jesus’ name, teaches in the synagogue and the hall of Tyrannus, and his ministry is accompanied by miracles, public repentance, and the spread of the Lord’s word. As Paul plans to travel through Macedonia and Achaia to Jerusalem and then Rome, Demetrius incites a riot over the threat to Artemis worship and the silversmiths’ trade, but the city clerk dismisses the assembly.

sections.heading: Paul’s Travel Plans and Demetrius’s Complaint
The Ephesian Riot and Its Dismissal

20.overview: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece, meets his companions in Troas, and restores Eutychus after the young man falls from an upper-room window. At Miletus, Paul tells the Ephesian elders of his coming trials, recounts his ministry, warns them about threats to the church, and bids them farewell.

sections.heading: Paul’s Address to the Ephesian Elders

21.overview: Paul travels to Jerusalem despite warnings from believers in Tyre and the prophet Agabus, and James and the elders advise him to join four men in a purification rite to counter rumors about his teaching. Jews from Asia incite a crowd against Paul in the temple, but Roman soldiers arrest him; as he is taken to the barracks, he asks permission to address the crowd.

sections.heading: Paul Meets James and the Elders
Paul Requests to Address the Crowd

22.overview: Paul addresses the Jerusalem crowd in Hebrew and recounts his Jewish upbringing, his encounter with Jesus on the road to Damascus, Ananias’s role, and his commission to witness to the Gentiles. The crowd erupts when Paul mentions the Gentiles, and the Roman commander orders him interrogated, then summons the Sanhedrin after learning Paul is a Roman citizen.

sections.heading: Paul’s encounter and commission in Damascus
The crowd’s reaction and Paul’s citizenship

23.overview: Before the Sanhedrin, Paul confronts High Priest Ananias and divides the council by declaring his hope in the resurrection, prompting the commander to remove him. After the Lord tells Paul he will testify in Rome, Paul’s nephew exposes a plot against him, and Claudius Lysias sends him under guard to Governor Felix in Caesarea.

24.overview: Ananias and Tertullus accuse Paul before Felix of stirring unrest and profaning the temple, while Paul denies the charges and identifies his faith in the Way and hope in the resurrection. Felix postpones judgment, later hears Paul speak about faith, righteousness, self-control, and judgment, and leaves him imprisoned when Festus succeeds him.

sections.heading: Felix Delays and Leaves Paul Imprisoned

25.overview: Festus hears the Jewish leaders’ charges against Paul in Caesarea, rejects their request to move the trial to Jerusalem, and sends Paul to Caesar after Paul appeals to the emperor. Later, Festus presents Paul’s case to King Agrippa and Bernice, explaining that he found no charge worthy of death but needs grounds to report to Caesar.

26.overview: Before King Agrippa, Paul recounts his Pharisaic past, his persecution of Jesus’ followers, and his encounter with the risen Jesus, who appoints him to bring Jews and Gentiles from darkness to God. Paul says his preaching fulfills the prophets’ message about the suffering and resurrection of the Christ, and after Festus and Agrippa respond, they conclude that Paul has done nothing deserving death or imprisonment but cannot release him because he has appealed to Caesar.

sections.heading: Paul’s background and hope in the resurrection
Paul’s encounter and commission from Jesus
Paul’s preaching and the prophets’ message

27.overview: Paul sails toward Italy under the guard of Julius, but worsening weather delays the voyage and the crew ignores Paul’s warning to remain in Crete. After a violent storm leaves the passengers without hope, Paul reports God’s promise that all aboard will survive, and the ship is wrecked near an island where everyone reaches land safely.

sections.heading: The voyage from Caesarea to Fair Havens
The sailors’ escape attempt and the meal

28.overview: On Malta, Paul survives a viper’s bite, heals Publius’s father and other islanders, and receives provisions before sailing on to Rome. In Rome, he meets with Jewish leaders, explains the hope of Israel, teaches about God’s kingdom and Jesus, and continues proclaiming freely for two years.
